paragraphs: The Manager of the Office of the National Chairman (ONC) of the National Resistance Movement (NRM), Hajjat Hadijah Namyalo Uzeiye, has called on Ugandans to protect the country’s peace and stability as Uganda prepares to mark 64 years of independence.

Addressing the media on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, Namyalo said political independence can only be meaningful when citizens are able to live in peace, enjoy their freedoms and participate in the development of their country.

Uganda attained independence from Britain on October 9, 1962. Namyalo said that while this was a major milestone in the country’s history, the years that followed showed that political independence alone did not guarantee lasting peace and stability.
“Uganda attained political independence on 9th October 1962. But the painful reality is that independence did not immediately give Ugandans peace, military security and stability,” Namyalo said.

She reflected on Uganda’s post-independence history, including periods of political instability, military coups and armed conflict, and urged Ugandans to learn from the past as they work towards a peaceful future.
Namyalo said the National Resistance Movement’s rise to power in 1986 came at a time when Uganda had experienced years of political instability and conflict.
According to Namyalo, President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni’s government focused on restoring peace and security, rebuilding state institutions and creating an environment for national development.
“When President Museveni assumed leadership in 1986, he inherited a country deeply damaged by years of conflict and political turmoil,” she said.

paragraphs: The Manager of the Office of the National Chairman (ONC), Hajjat Hadijah Namyalo Uzeiye, this afternoon joined fellow members of the NRM Central Executive Committee (CEC) for the NRM Parliamentary Caucus meeting at Kololo.
The meeting, presided over by President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni, brought together senior NRM leaders and Members of Parliament to discuss various issues of national importance.
Namyalo attended the meeting in her capacity as a member of the party’s Central Executive Committee.

The Parliamentary Caucus provides a platform for NRM leaders and legislators to discuss key matters concerning the party, Parliament and the country, as well as coordinate positions on issues under consideration.
The meeting at Kololo forms part of the party’s ongoing consultations on matters affecting national governance and development.

paragraphs: The Manager of the Office of the National Chairman (ONC), Hajjat Hadijah Namyalo Uzeiye, has joined the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in celebrating its 96th National Day, extending warm congratulations to the Saudi Government and its people.
Namyalo used the occasion to reaffirm the valued friendship between Uganda and Saudi Arabia and expressed optimism about the continued growth of relations between the two countries.

title: Hajjati Hadiya Namyalo Distributes Seeds and Fertilizers to Farmers in Maddu Ahead of Planting Season
excerpt: The Office of the National Chairman (ONC), led by Senior Presidential Advisor Hajjat Hadijah Namyalo Uzeiye, popularly known as Chief Muzzukulu, has distributed seeds and fertilizers to farmers at Maddu Town Council Playgrounds ahead of the upcoming planting season. paragraphs: The Office of the National Chairman (ONC), led by Senior Presidential Advisor Hajjat Hadijah Namyalo Uzeiye, popularly known as Chief Muzzukulu, has distributed seeds and fertilizers to farmers at Maddu Town Council Playgrounds ahead of the upcoming planting season.
The initiative is aimed at supporting farmers with essential agricultural inputs to help them prepare for the new season, improve production and strengthen household incomes.
Namyalo said supporting farmers with quality seeds and fertilizers is important in enabling communities to increase agricultural productivity and make farming a more reliable source of income.
The distribution also forms part of ONC’s wider grassroots empowerment efforts, with a focus on helping ordinary Ugandans access practical tools and resources that can improve their livelihoods.
Farmers gathered at Maddu Town Council Playgrounds to receive the agricultural inputs as they prepare their gardens for planting.
Namyalo encouraged beneficiaries to make proper use of the seeds and fertilizers and focus on productive farming that can provide food for their families while generating income from surplus produce.
The initiative comes as farmers prepare for the planting season and follows continued calls for improved access to affordable and quality agricultural inputs across the country.

title: Prime Minister Nabbanja Joins Spiritual Revival Honouring Uganda’s Fallen Liberation Heroes
excerpt: Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja has joined religious leaders, liberation veterans, families of fallen heroes and citizens at the Office of the National Chairman (ONC) in Kyambogo for the Spiritual Revival of the Fallen Warriors. paragraphs: Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja has joined religious leaders, liberation veterans, families of fallen heroes and citizens at the Office of the National Chairman (ONC) in Kyambogo for the Spiritual Revival of the Fallen Warriors.
The gathering brings together Ugandans to remember and honour men and women who lost their lives during Uganda’s liberation struggle and to reflect on their contribution to the country.
Nabbanja’s participation highlights the significance of the commemoration, which combines prayer, remembrance and reflection on Uganda’s history.

Religious leaders led participants in prayers for the fallen heroes, their families and the country, while veterans and families gathered to remember the sacrifices made during the liberation struggle.
The event also provides an opportunity for younger generations to learn about Uganda’s history and understand the experiences and sacrifices of those who participated in the liberation struggle.
Through the Spiritual Revival of the Fallen Warriors, participants are paying tribute to the fallen while keeping their stories and contributions part of the country’s national memory.

title: ONC Manager Hajjat Namyalo Calls for Spiritual Revival to Honour Uganda’s Fallen Liberation Heroes

paragraphs: The Manager of the Office of the National Chairman (ONC), Hajjat Hadijah Namyalo, has called upon Ugandans of all faiths to join a spiritual revival ahead of President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni’s birthday on September 15.

This year’s commemoration, themed “Spiritual Revival of Our Fallen Warriors,” will honour NRA heroes who sacrificed their lives during Uganda’s liberation struggle while bringing Ugandans together in prayer and reflection.

Hajjat Namyalo said the occasion will also provide an opportunity to seek God’s guidance as the country continues to address challenges affecting its people, including poverty, unemployment and access to quality healthcare.
The main commemoration will take place at ONC Kyambogo on September 15 and is expected to bring together religious leaders, liberation veterans, families of fallen heroes and other Ugandans.

As the country remembers fallen heroes, including Fred Rwigyema, Gen. Elly Tumwine and others, Hajjat Namyalo encouraged Ugandans to reflect on the country’s history and recognise the sacrifices that contributed to shaping modern Uganda.

She also called for continued efforts to create economic opportunities and improve livelihoods, particularly for the Bazzukulu, while preserving the history and contribution of those who participated in Uganda’s liberation struggle.

paragraphs: The Manager of the Office of the National Chairman (ONC), Hajjat Hadijah Namyalo Uzeiye, has called on Ugandans of all faiths to join a nationwide spiritual revival ahead of President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni’s birthday on September 15.

This year’s commemoration will be held under the theme “Spiritual Revival of Our Fallen Warriors,” celebrating the men and women of the National Resistance Army (NRA) who sacrificed their lives for Uganda’s peace and stability.

Hajjat Namyalo said the occasion will not only honour the country’s heroes but also unite Ugandans in prayer as the nation seeks God’s guidance in overcoming challenges such as poverty, unemployment and limited access to quality healthcare.
The main celebration will take place at the ONC headquarters in Kyambogo on September 15, bringing together religious leaders, veterans, families of fallen heroes and members of the public.
Namyalo encouraged Ugandans to remember the sacrifices of heroes including Fred Rwigyema, Gen. Elly Tumwine and many others whose dedication helped shape modern Uganda.
She said the commemoration is also an opportunity for the Bazzukulu to renew their commitment to patriotism, unity and creating better opportunities for future generations.
“As we honour our fallen heroes, let us also recommit ourselves to building a stronger, more prosperous Uganda for every citizen,” Hajjat Namyalo said.

title: ONC Calls for Review of Agricultural Input Distribution to Support Farmers Across Uganda
excerpt: The Office of the National Chairman (ONC) of the NRM has called for an urgent review of Uganda’s agricultural input support and distribution framework, citing concerns over the rising cost and limited accessibility of quality farming inputs, particularly coffee seedlings and other planting materials. Speaking at the ON
paragraphs: The Office of the National Chairman (ONC) of the NRM has called for an urgent review of Uganda’s agricultural input support and distribution framework, citing concerns over the rising cost and limited accessibility of quality farming inputs, particularly coffee seedlings and other planting materials.

Speaking at the ONC offices in Kyambogo, ONC Manager Hajjat Hadijah Namyalo Uzeiye said farmers from different parts of the country continue to raise concerns about the affordability, quality, timely delivery and accessibility of agricultural inputs.

Hajjat Namyalo said Uganda’s economic transformation efforts require farmers to have access to the basic inputs needed to increase production and household incomes. She called for an agricultural support system that responds directly to farmers’ needs and reflects the different farming conditions across the country.
She proposed a region-specific approach that considers Uganda’s different agro-ecological zones, suitable crops, planting seasons and the actual needs of farmers in each area.

The ONC also called for stronger coordination between agricultural input support and financing under the Parish Development Model (PDM). According to the office, access to productive financing should be complemented by affordable agricultural inputs, extension services and reliable markets to help households move from subsistence production into the money economy.

Hajjat Namyalo further called upon the Government and relevant institutions to strengthen and, where necessary, reinstate the strategic distribution of affordable, quality and climate-suitable seedlings and other agricultural inputs.

The ONC said improving access to the right inputs at the right time would help farmers increase production, strengthen household incomes and make better use of Government programmes aimed at expanding participation in the money economy.

title: President Museveni Calls on NRM Leaders to Strengthen Implementation of Government Programmes
excerpt: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni addressed the NRM Caucus at Kololo, urging leaders to return to the National Resistance Movement’s core working methods and closely follow up on Government programmes to ensure they reach the intended beneficiaries. The President emphasised the importance of effectively implementing the
paragraphs: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni addressed the NRM Caucus at Kololo, urging leaders to return to the National Resistance Movement’s core working methods and closely follow up on Government programmes to ensure they reach the intended beneficiaries.

The President emphasised the importance of effectively implementing the Parish Development Model (PDM), noting that the programme must reach communities and help households improve their incomes and livelihoods.

President Museveni also addressed the protection of Uganda’s wetlands, stressing that these important natural resources must be preserved. He called on people occupying wetlands to move away from them and adopt alternative income-generating activities.

In areas such as Busoga, Bukedi and Kigezi, the President said the Government will support affected communities to transition to fish farming. This approach is intended to provide alternative sources of income while protecting water resources that can also support irrigation and agricultural production.

President Museveni urged leaders to remain actively involved in monitoring Government programmes and ensuring that development initiatives deliver meaningful benefits to communities across the country.

title: President Museveni Calls for Wealth Preservation and Better Healthcare Support for Older Persons
excerpt: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni officiated at the International Day of Older Persons celebrations at State House Entebbe, where he encouraged older people to embrace modern approaches to wealth preservation and inheritance. The President noted that some older people divide their property among their children, which ca
paragraphs: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni officiated at the International Day of Older Persons celebrations at State House Entebbe, where he encouraged older people to embrace modern approaches to wealth preservation and inheritance.

The President noted that some older people divide their property among their children, which can gradually fragment family wealth. He encouraged families to consider modern inheritance approaches, including shareholding arrangements, that can allow assets and businesses to remain productive while benefiting future generations.

President Museveni said the Government’s objective is to help older people who have accumulated wealth preserve it, while supporting those without sufficient income or assets to improve their livelihoods through existing Government programmes.
He further announced plans to develop a Parish Development Model (PDM) programme tailored to the needs of older persons after the Government concludes its financial commitments related to AFCON.

The President also highlighted healthcare as a major concern for older people, who often face increased medical needs and expenses. He proposed that the Government sponsor the training and recruitment of geriatricians across the country, with the goal of having a specialist in each district to provide regular and free medical support to older persons.

President Museveni emphasised the importance of combining financial security, sustainable wealth management and accessible healthcare to improve the welfare and quality of life of Uganda’s older population.

title: President Museveni Highlights Value Addition, Industrialisation and East African Integration
excerpt: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni has emphasised Uganda’s commitment to developing its oil refinery while maintaining cooperation with Tanzania on regional energy infrastructure, including projects linked to Tanga. The President noted that having more refineries within the region would support Africa’s broader developme
paragraphs: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni has emphasised Uganda’s commitment to developing its oil refinery while maintaining cooperation with Tanzania on regional energy infrastructure, including projects linked to Tanga.

The President noted that having more refineries within the region would support Africa’s broader development goals rather than create unnecessary competition. He stressed that African countries should focus on adding value to their natural resources, expanding industrial production and building larger integrated markets.

President Museveni has consistently advocated for value addition as an important step towards creating jobs, increasing incomes and enabling African countries to benefit more from their resources instead of relying heavily on the export of raw materials.
He also highlighted the importance of deeper East African integration, describing political integration as a long-term strategic matter for the region.

According to the President, stronger regional cooperation and integration can help East African countries build larger markets, strengthen their economies and collectively address the region’s long-term development and strategic interests.

title: President Museveni Calls for Protection of Marriage, Culture and Indigenous Knowledge
excerpt: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni has called upon cultural leaders to play a stronger role in addressing issues surrounding marriage, responsible family life and the preservation of Uganda’s cultural heritage. The President encouraged communities to reflect on traditional approaches to marriage, noting that established
paragraphs: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni has called upon cultural leaders to play a stronger role in addressing issues surrounding marriage, responsible family life and the preservation of Uganda’s cultural heritage.

The President encouraged communities to reflect on traditional approaches to marriage, noting that established cultural practices provided clear structures for families and contributed to maintaining social order.

President Museveni also raised concern about HIV prevalence in some parts of Uganda, including Western Uganda. He pointed to Karamoja’s strong cultural practices around marriage as an example worth studying when examining social behaviour and community structures related to family life.

Beyond marriage and family, the President emphasised the importance of protecting Uganda’s languages, cultural practices, indigenous knowledge and traditional science. He warned that valuable local knowledge could disappear if deliberate efforts are not made to document, preserve and pass it on to future generations.

President Museveni cited the preservation of Ankole long-horned cattle as an example of safeguarding indigenous resources. He recalled his efforts to maintain the breed despite earlier advice favouring modern alternatives and also referred to having sold some of the cattle to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa.

The President called for greater attention to Uganda’s indigenous science, traditional crafts, cultural practices and heritage, describing them as important elements of national identity that should be protected for future generations.

title: President Museveni Highlights Tourism, Wealth Creation and Environmental Protection
excerpt: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni addressed celebrations marking World Tourism Day at Mbale S.S. Grounds, where he encouraged Ugandans to embrace the four sectors of wealth creation and take advantage of the economic opportunities available within the tourism industry. The President highlighted Uganda’s diverse tourism
paragraphs: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni addressed celebrations marking World Tourism Day at Mbale S.S. Grounds, where he encouraged Ugandans to embrace the four sectors of wealth creation and take advantage of the economic opportunities available within the tourism industry.

The President highlighted Uganda’s diverse tourism attractions, including the snow-capped Rwenzori Mountains, wildlife, natural landscapes and favourable climate. He noted that these resources give the country significant potential to attract international and domestic visitors and generate more income from tourism.

President Museveni described tourism as an important global industry and called for Uganda to position itself to benefit more from the sector by protecting its attractions, improving infrastructure and increasing economic participation among local communities.

He also emphasised the connection between tourism, agriculture, electricity generation and environmental conservation. The President warned against the destruction of wetlands and other natural resources, noting that environmental degradation threatens water sources, agriculture, tourism and the country’s long-term development.

President Museveni further called for the extension of last-mile infrastructure to areas such as Bududa and Manjiya. He said improved infrastructure would enhance accessibility, connect communities and support tourism and other economic activities.

The President also acknowledged the efforts of the Uganda Wildlife Authority (UWA) and the Ministry of Tourism in promoting and developing Uganda’s tourism sector, while encouraging them to continue strengthening their work across the country.

title: President Museveni Welcomes Stronger Uganda–Japan Cooperation and Investment
excerpt: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni received Ambassador Takahashi Misako, Japan’s Assistant Minister for African Affairs, and her delegation for discussions on strengthening cooperation between Uganda and Japan. During the meeting, President Museveni expressed appreciation to the Japanese Government for its continued supp
paragraphs: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni received Ambassador Takahashi Misako, Japan’s Assistant Minister for African Affairs, and her delegation for discussions on strengthening cooperation between Uganda and Japan.

During the meeting, President Museveni expressed appreciation to the Japanese Government for its continued support to Uganda, particularly in infrastructure development. He highlighted major projects supported by Japan, including the Kampala Flyover and the Source of the Nile Bridge in Jinja, among other initiatives.

The President also discussed Uganda’s plans to acquire road construction and maintenance equipment directly through the Japanese Government, without involving middlemen. He explained that the Government’s objective is to ensure that every urban centre has access to its own road equipment rather than relying on machinery shared across an entire district.
President Museveni further invited more Japanese companies to explore investment opportunities in Uganda, noting that stronger trade, investment and economic cooperation would benefit both countries.
The President emphasised that Uganda’s broader objective is to promote prosperity and improve household incomes, while building mutually beneficial economic partnerships with countries such as Japan.
He noted that greater prosperity in both Uganda and Japan would create opportunities for businesses, communities and citizens of the two countries.

title: President Museveni Directs Faster Preparations for AFCON 2027
excerpt: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni met with CAF Secretary General Samson Adamu and members of the National AFCON Task Force at State House Entebbe for an update on Uganda’s preparations to co-host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) alongside Kenya and Tanzania. The National AFCON Task Force, led by Prime Minister Rob
paragraphs: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni met with CAF Secretary General Samson Adamu and members of the National AFCON Task Force at State House Entebbe for an update on Uganda’s preparations to co-host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) alongside Kenya and Tanzania.
The National AFCON Task Force, led by Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja, briefed the President on the progress being made ahead of the continental football tournament.

President Museveni directed the relevant Government institutions and agencies to accelerate preparations, with particular attention to key infrastructure required for the tournament. These include training grounds, roads, airport facilities and accommodation, especially in the upcountry cities expected to host AFCON activities.
The President emphasised the need to complete the necessary works within the required timelines and ensure that all facilities meet the standards expected for the tournament.

President Museveni also announced plans to engage his counterparts in Kenya and Tanzania on a proposed single visa arrangement for AFCON 2027. The initiative would seek to make movement between the three host countries easier for visitors during the tournament.

Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania are jointly preparing to host AFCON 2027, requiring close regional coordination as the three countries work towards delivering the necessary facilities and services for the competition.

title: My Birthday Reflections: Africa’s Future and Uganda’s Petroleum Security
excerpt: Fellow Ugandans, especially the Bazzukulu. Greetings. I want to thank the 8 million well-wishers that sent me congratulations on my 82nd birthday on the 15th of September, 2026. Those well-wishes and God’s blessings will push me and Maama for another just 18 years to reach 100 years of age and for Maama to reach 96…
paragraphs: Fellow Ugandans, especially the Bazzukulu. Greetings. I want to thank the 8 million well-wishers that sent me congratulations on my 82nd birthday on the 15th of September, 2026. Those well-wishes and God’s blessings will push me and Maama for another just 18 years to reach 100 years of age and for Maama to reach 96 years. In those remaining years, I appeal to the Africans, if they want to avoid future calamity, to work on the 3 historical missions not yet attained. These are: prosperity for the Africans through integrating the African common market to help the wealth creators expand; strategic security against all threats through the political integration of the continent where possible, such as is the case with the East African Federation; in all this using undugu (the brotherhood) of the four linguistic groups of the 1.5bn Africans- the Niger-Congo (the Bantu and Kwa), the Nilo-Saharan (Cushitic, Nilotic, etc.), the Afro-Asiatic (Arabic, Tigrinya, Amhara) and the Khoisan.

It is the fulfilment of these historical missions, that will guarantee our prosperity and strategic security. In the meantime, some Kenya Media People decided, recently, to put pilipili (red pepper) in what I said recently when I was laying the Foundation stone of the 320 million litres oil storage centre at Buyala.

The real story is that when we were fighting Idi Amin, among other things, we used to say that he had destroyed governance in Uganda by putting abatasoma (the ones that did not go to school) in charge of running the affairs of the Country. Indeed, when we defeated Idi Amin, we put back the civil servants in charge of running the administration of the Country. It was much later that we discovered that those civil servants (PS, Commissioners, etc.), were ruining the Country. In, for instance, the matter of purchasing Petroleum products for the country- a whole Country-Uganda- I did not know that these wonderful People were buying those products through middle-men in Kenya by tendering to those middlemen.

It was a Kenyan Senator called Jirongo who told me this around 2019. I immediately tasked the then Minister Irene Muloni to sort out that mess. Nevertheless, nothing happened, until 2023 when we linked up with a group known as Vitol that has refineries in different parts of the World and are also bulk suppliers. Our initial agreement with them on the 18th of August 2023, provided that we buy per metric tonne as follows:
Diesel: Old price—USD 118 New price—USD 83
Petrol: Old Price—USD 97.5 New Price—USD 61.5
Aviation fuel: Old price—USD 114.25 New price—USD 79.25

I want to thank H.E Ruto because he prevailed over some actors in Kenya who were trying to resist. That is how we got our new arrangement and the Kenya Government allows us to pump our products through the Kenya oil pipeline in which the Kenya Government allowed us to have shares of 20.15%. We are very happy with the Kenya Government of President Ruto on this matter.

title: Hajjat Hadijah Namyalo Uzeiye Meets MUBS Principal Ahead of Muslim Inter-University Games
excerpt: The Manager of the Office of the National Chairman (ONC), Hajjat Hadijah Namyalo Uzeiye, has visited Makerere University Business School (MUBS) Principal Prof. Moses Muhwezi ahead of the upcoming Muslim Inter-University Games. During the meeting, the two discussed youth empowerment and the important role universities c
paragraphs: The Manager of the Office of the National Chairman (ONC), Hajjat Hadijah Namyalo Uzeiye, has visited Makerere University Business School (MUBS) Principal Prof. Moses Muhwezi ahead of the upcoming Muslim Inter-University Games.

During the meeting, the two discussed youth empowerment and the important role universities can play in preparing young people to become productive and economically independent after completing their studies.
Prof. Muhwezi commended Namyalo for her continued efforts to empower young Ugandans, particularly through initiatives aimed at promoting entrepreneurship, skills development and self-reliance.

He noted that these efforts closely align with MUBS’s mission of producing graduates who are not only academically prepared but also capable of creating opportunities for themselves and contributing to Uganda’s economic development.
Namyalo reaffirmed her commitment to supporting young people, commonly referred to as the Bazzukulu, and encouraging them to take advantage of available opportunities to improve their livelihoods.

The visit comes ahead of the Muslim Inter-University Games, which will bring together students from different universities through sport while promoting unity, interaction and talent development among young people.

paragraphs: The Office of the NRM National Chairman (ONC) headquarters was a hub of strategic engagement today as ONC Manager, Hajjat Hadijah Namyalo Uzeiye, welcomed a high-powered delegation from Buikwe District.

The courtesy visit brought together Hon. Mutebi David Ronnie (MP, Buikwe South), along with NRM flag bearers Badru Kabuye Mpoza (Njeru Municipality) and Isaac Mulindwa Ssozi (Lugazi Municipality). The ONC team and Buikwe leaders reaffirmed their dedication to grassroots mobilization and inclusive development, ensuring that the NRM continues to grow stronger and more vibrant at every level.
Together, these efforts are shaping a united front and building a solid foundation for sustainable progress and success in 2026 and beyond.

The upcoming event will feature a range of activities, including the distribution of capital items to support individuals and groups in starting or boosting their businesses. The day will also be filled with entertainment, with popular artists such as Gravity Omutujju set to perform.

paragraphs: The Senior Presidential Advisor and Head of the Office of the National Chairperson, Hajjat Hadijah Namyalo Uzeiye, yesterday hosted Mr. Phillip Kakuru, the Senior Presidential Advisor on Trade, at her office.

During the cordial meeting, the two dignitaries held in-depth discussions on a variety of national issues, with a key focus on empowering Jajja’s Bazzukulu—an initiative aimed at uplifting and equipping the youth with practical skills and opportunities to foster self-reliance and national development.

Their engagement highlighted the continued commitment of the Office of the National Chairperson to collaborate across government sectors in promoting socio-economic transformation, especially among the younger generation.

paragraphs: On the preceding day, Mr. Julius Nakiyi, a prospective parliamentary candidate for the Budadiri East constituency, paid a formal courtesy visit to the Office of the National Resistance Movement (NRM) National Chairman. The meeting facilitated productive deliberations focused on establishing strategic collaborative initiatives.

These initiatives are designed to ensure the NRM’s electoral success within the Sironko District and to secure a substantial electoral mandate of 90% for His Excellency President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni in the 2026 general elections.
